title: Google Fi adds support for a second 5G network, won't say which one
gist: Google Fi's new 'super network' makes it a dual-carrier MVNO again, switching between T-Mobile 5G and an unnamed second network that the author guesses is Verizon. The feature is limited to Pixel 9-11 phones on eSIM, at no extra cost on premium plans.

insights.claim: Google Fi's 'super network' lets phones hop between T-Mobile 5G and a second US 5G network, making Fi dual-carrier in the US again after years as a T-Mobile-only MVNO following T-Mobile's absorption of Sprint.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: T-Mobile loses exclusivity on a notable MVNO; a wholesale win for AT&T or Verizon.
insights.locator: With the super network, Google Fi

insights.claim: Google declined to name Fi's second network partner; based on coverage maps, Ars's Ryan Whitwam guesses Verizon over AT&T.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Possible Verizon wholesale deal with Google; watch for confirmation.
insights.locator: We know one of them is T-Mobile

insights.claim: MVNOs increasingly hide which networks they use; Google's Fi FAQ no longer even confirms T-Mobile, despite Fi historically touting top prioritization on T-Mobile towers.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Reduced transparency in MVNO network relationships.

insights.claim: Fi network switching is initially limited to Pixel 9, Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 phones configured with Fi as eSIM and other SIMs disabled; other devices get access in 2027.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Feature used as a Pixel hardware differentiator.

insights.claim: Super network support rolls out at no additional cost on Google Fi's Unlimited Premium and Flexible plans.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Value add without price increase, competitive pressure on MVNO peers.
